title: Article 164 — Other provisions as to Ministers

content.overview: Article 164 provides that the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and the other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister; Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State; a Minister who for any period of six consecutive months is not a member of the Legislature of the State ceases to be a Minister at the expiration of that period; and salaries and allowances of Ministers are as determined by the State Legislature by law. Special provisions apply for Tribal Welfare Ministers in certain States.
content.glance: CM appointed by Governor; other Ministers on CM’s advice. Pleasure of Governor. Collective responsibility to Legislative Assembly. 6-month membership rule.
content.study:
Article 164 is the State counterpart of Article 75:
- CM appointed by Governor; other Ministers on CM’s advice.
- Pleasure of the Governor.
- Collective responsibility to the Legislative Assembly (not to a Legislative Council).
- Six consecutive months without membership of the State Legislature → ceases to be Minister.
- Salaries by State Legislature by law.
- Special clause for Minister in charge of tribal welfare in certain States (e.g. Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha as provided).

Examination: parallel to Art 75; responsibility to Assembly only; 6-month rule; tribal welfare Minister in specified States.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. CM: appointed by Governor.
2. Other Ministers: appointed by Governor on advice of CM.
3. Hold office during pleasure of Governor.
4. Collective responsibility to the Legislative Assembly.
5. Six consecutive months without Legislature membership → ceases to be Minister.
6. Special tribal-welfare Minister provision in certain States.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the main provisions of Article 164.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 164, the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and the other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State. A Minister who is not a member of the State Legislature for six consecutive months ceases to be a Minister. Salaries and allowances are determined by the State Legislature by law. Special provision is made for a Minister in charge of tribal welfare in certain States.

examTips: Parallel to Art 75; collective responsibility to Assembly; 6-month rule.

keyTakeaways: Art 164: CM/Ministers; pleasure; collective responsibility to Assembly.
